svg.title: How a verdict is decided
svg.desc: Left: one comparison is four launches on the same machine, in the order incumbent, candidate, candidate, incumbent. The gain is the average of the two candidate-minus-incumbent differences, measured on log tokens per second, so it is a ratio. If the two incumbent launches differ by more than the noise allows, the verdict is VOID_DRIFT and the pair is thrown away. A gain that reaches the threshold, with the quality gate and the guards held, is PROMOTED. A run with no calibration or no incumbent yet is INCONCLUSIVE. A gain below the threshold, or a failed quality gate or guard, is REJECTED. The threshold is the larger of 2% and 3.2 times the noise between launches. Right: in a simulation with illustrative noise numbers, where a try counts as promoted only when the first comparison passed and a second one six simulated hours later confirmed it, a candidate with no real gain was promoted in 0.01% of tries, a 6% gain in 35.3%, an 8% gain in 64.0%, a 10% gain in 85.0% and a 12% gain in 93.6%.
